utterances.text: And can I ask you about this particular statement contained in the report. Do you recall putting it anywhere in this report -- in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The last two sentences which I have just read out to you.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the sentence regarding the search and cleaning of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me put that to you: Do you agree that this document, Mr. Bezruchenko, suggests, again, that the people present in the village had come pursuant to the order or with the authority of the president? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you also agree that the document suggests that no one else should know about the presence of the people?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that in the course of your investigation, or the investigation of the Office of the Prosecutor, you had interviewed Mr. -- or Major Mitre Despodov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the course of this interview, he also gave you information about the telephone conversation which he had with the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he indicated to you, inter alia, that he had been asked by the president who he was and asked about what was happening in the village or around the village at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that in the course of a further interview, this time with Mr. Buckovski, former Minister of Defence, Mr. Buckovski had indicated to you that the people who had come in the village were, for some of them, members of the -- or at least one of them a member of the security of the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that in the course of your interviews with various members of the army at the time, you were informed that the various level of the military chain of command had not been informed that the operation was to be started? Do you agree with that, that you had interviewed a number of people who indicated to you that they had not been informed about the preparations of the operation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As has transpired from these interviews, and by and large these statements supported by the available documents, Major Despodov, in fact, did not receive any definitive order by the president or by General Mitrovski to carry out any action in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that Mr. Despodov provided the fire support that was necessary for the operation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you know also from your interviews that General Stambolski and also Colonel Kopacev, who were in the chain of command, had not been informed about the preparations for the operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would appear from the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that when I asked about the question of the president's involvement in the operation, Mr. Mitrovski, General Mitrovksi, indicated to you the following: "The 12 August, I didn't issue any order, and I didn't need to establish a commission which would investigate whether the president was involved or not. The Chief of the General Staff and the Ministry of Defence were informed the ball was in their court. I wasn't asked about it, nor anybody called me to ask for a opinion." Do you recall that statement, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, what Mr. Mitrovski indicates in his statement is that the responsibility to talk to the president about this particular matter was with his superior in the General Staff and the Ministry of Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's another piece of information which you had in your possession about the involvement or the authority responsible for the events in Ljuboten, and you knew that the matter of Ljuboten was dealt with not in the Ministry of Interior or in the Ministry of Defence, but at the presidential and command level. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, Mr. Mettraux. As I explained previously, there are no clear indications that Major Despodov received any orders either from the president or from General Mitrovksi as regards Ljuboten. This is a fact. Now, if there is any information to suggest that the authority responsible for the events of Ljuboten is some appropriate level, if your implication is in fact is that it is the president who is responsible, well, I don't really have any hard evidence suggesting that he gave any specific orders relating to Ljuboten. All that is just hearsay which is reflected in various documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look, for instance, at what is now Exhibit 1D246, please. This document, Mr. Bezruchenko, is part of a bigger document which is on your Rule 65 ter list as Rule 65 ter 216, and it's a daily log sheet. It comes from the archives of the OSCE, and it relates to the 12th of August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could ask the registry to turn to the third page after that document, please, and if we could have the English version as well, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, I will draw your attention to entry number 15 in that particular document. It says that: "Two meetings are ongoing on presidential and command level in order to find a solution for the Ljuboten problem." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this is pretty hard evidence to the effect that the matter of Ljuboten on the 12th of August was dealt with at the presidential and command level? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is it the evidence of the fact that meetings were, indeed, being held with the involvement of president and, perhaps, at the command level, but this is the only thing that I can say about there particular entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko -- perhaps I should ask you this first: Do you agree that in the course of preparing your report, you've reviewed a vast number of media reports and media material?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also relied on a large quantity of such material for the purpose of preparing your original report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a significant amount of the material, and, of course, not all of it could be reflected in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would know also from reviewing that material that the fact that the president had ordered the operation in Ljuboten had been aired in the press as well. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this particular fact, I don't think so. I don't think I saw any specific media report suggesting that president directly ordered operation in Ljuboten. But if even that were the case, well, I don't think that this media report would carry any more significance and value in terms of credibility than a report by the Ministry of Defence or the General Staff for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D531.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is it a media report which comes from your collections, so I'll ask you first: Do you recall reviewing that particular document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please kindly -- yes. Let me see. Actually, I don't remember, but could we go perhaps through the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could please turn to the next page, or perhaps scroll it to the bottom for Mr. Bezruchenko and then turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing that document, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Does that help refresh your memory? Do you recall seeing that document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the book by Ms. Biljana Plavsic. I read it, but I don't really recall this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we could turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask you to focus on the second paragraph of that particular document. It says the following: "The then-state leadership claimed that there was an armed group in the village which planted a pressure-activated mine which killed eight Macedonian soldiers the day before the village was attacked. "The order for Macedonian soldiers to engage the Albanian group came from the then-supreme commander of the Macedonian army, President Boris Trajkovski." Do you recall seeing that statement, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you would agree that this is nowhere to be found in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is perhaps mentioned in my report, particularly in the chronology because I widely used various media reports; but mentioning this particular statement in the section related to Ljuboten, there was no point, really, because essentially this is a issue of serious significance. It would be extremely irresponsible on my part to plant anything in the -- anything like this in the section on developments in Ljuboten, based on this source only.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We can remove the document from the screen at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'd like to turn now to something quite different, and that is the issue of what you say was an armed conflict in Macedonia in the year of 2001. There's a few general matters which I would like to go through with you. First, you have indicated in your evidence-in-chief, though not in your report, that the definition of what constitutes an armed conflict for the purpose of your report is based on your understanding of that concept as defined in military doctrine. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my understanding is actually based on a number of sources, including various military manuals, various scholarly works, books on military history, and these kind of things. But one of those sources which I used and which I mentioned to you previously was this particular one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the particular one you are referring to, Mr. Bezruchenko, would be the definition that is provided for in the DoD Military Dictionary. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that on the basis of this definition, which we've read already, an armed conflict with oppose two or more side that are fighting each other. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that those sides would generally be known or referred to as being parties to an armed conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your report, you suggest that the parties to the armed conflict were, on the one hand, the National Liberation Army, and, on the other, the Macedonian security forces, comprising the army and the security forces of the MOI. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your report at paragraph 14, you suggest that the Macedonian conflict, and I quote: "Had certain common features with other similar conflicts in the world." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate what armed conflict or armed conflict you suggest shared common features with this particular conflict which you say would render them comparable?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could name perhaps a number of them. This could be the conflict in Kosovo; this could be the conflict in Algeria between the French army and the Algerian insurgents in, I think, 1954 and 1960s; and a number of conflicts of similar nature in Latin America.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is your expert evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, that those conflict would be comparable to the conflict in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In their major features, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to pause before answering questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you had a general understanding of what the concept of armed conflict means in legal terms?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, the purpose of my report was not the legal analysis of the conflict. This is an entirely different matter. I was not trying to provide legal analysis of what was happening in Macedonia in 2001. I think it is pretty clear from my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. My question was more general in kind. Do you agree that you had a general understanding of what the concept of armed conflict meant in legal terms and in particular what it meant before this Tribunal? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I have mentioned previously, I have studied various books and various sources related to military history and the theory of the conflict in general. So, if you are implying that I had any knowledge of various legal theories, yes, I did. If your question is whether I actually applied these theories to my report, the question [sic] is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me take it in two steps. Is it correct that colleagues, members of your team of the Office of the Prosecutor, explained to you what the concept of armed conflict meant in legal terms and what the relevant factors or facts to establish such a matter were in relation to the law of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had various discussions related to the report; and whether this explanations actually were made in the course of these discussions, well, I don't remember. Perhaps, it was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were also made aware, weren't you, about the most important, perhaps, decisions and judgments of this Tribunal about what an armed conflict meant, in legal terms. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. It was not really the focus of my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that it was brought to your attention that a number of factors or facts were relative to establishing an armed conflict, and that those criterias had been identified in various judgments of the ICTY? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is correct, Mr. Mettraux, but I would like to emphasise, again, that it was not really the focus of my attention. I don't remember, well, really studying these judgments for the purpose of writing my reports. Actually, I did not really study these judgments. I was simply not interested. It was not my interest at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that your colleagues of the Office of the Prosecutor, in particular, identified for you the criteria -- or criterias which had been taken into account in the Limaj trial judgment to establish what, under the jurisdiction of the Tribunal, is it an armed conflict? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you knew and understood that the two main criteria relevant to this matter, that of an armed conflict in law, were requirement of sufficient organisation and a requirement of sufficient intensity in military exchanges. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, as I mentioned previously , and you seem to be bringing it back to the point which I have to repeat again - I did not write my report with any legal analysis in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bezruchenko, the question is slightly different. The question or my question, if it wasn't clear, is whether this fact and criterias were brought to your attention.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware, Mr. Bezruchenko, that one of the factor relevant to the legal definition of an armed conflict is the ability of the parties to carry out certain types of military operations? Were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, with all my due respect again, let me repeat, that the legal definition of the armed conflict was not really a matter of my concern. I hope that sufficiently answers my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your answer is "no."

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that prior to preparing your report which we are now discussing, you had never been asked to make a study of whether an armed conflict had existed in a particular place? Is that correct that was your first such report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for my Ph.D., no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And had you been asked by the Office of the Prosecutor to prepare any such report in the context of your work?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I kindly ask to you qualify your question, Mr. Mettraux. What do you mean by "such report"?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Had you been asked, prior to preparing this report by the Office of the Prosecutor, to prepare a report as to whether or not there had been an armed conflict in a particular location or country?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first report of this kind which I produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Have you published any academic paper in relation to the subject matter; namely, the concept of armed conflict in military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have published a number of articles which are related to the subject of the conflict in Bosnia, but papers, as you term them academic papers, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those papers, the ones that are referred to in your curriculum vitae, as you indicated, were not papers discussing the definition of the concept of armed conflict in military doctrine. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your report and in evidence, you have stated your belief that the conflict started in January of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps for the sake of clarity, would you be able to indicate on what date, if any particular date in January, you say the conflict started?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I kindly refer you to page 1 of the section 5 of my report. Paragraph 2 on this page says the following: "The armed conflict in 2001 commenced with the first attack by the NLA on January 22nd against the police station in the village of Tearce near Tetovo. Assailants used rocket propelled grenades and automatic weapons. "One police officer was killed and three others wounded. The NLA claimed the responsibility for the attack in communique number 4 on January 23rd, 2001."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bezruchenko, and we will come back in a minute to that particular paragraph. Is it correct -- or rather, let me ask you this: In your report, you suggested that the armed conflict had lasted at least between January and September 2001. There was an internal armed conflict in the Republic of Macedonia..." -- sorry, "at least between January and September of 2001." The rest is not from paragraph 10. Is that correct, that's the duration which you have identified as relevant?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, is that all through that time, that is, between January and September of 2001, there was, in fact, an armed conflict on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be more precise, as you are aware, Mr. Mettraux, the conflict, by and large, was terminated, at least on paper, on 13 August 2001. On this day, the Ohrid Agreement was signed which, among other things, stipulated the end of the hostilities. But, in reality, the cease-fire violations continued for a long time after this agreement was signed. The reason why I specifically selected September for the conceptual end of the conflict was that on the 26th of September, one of the warring parties, namely, the NLA, made a statement about its disbandment following the end of the operation Essential Harvest which, again, as you were aware, was meant to collect the NLA weapons in return for certain political concessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for this explanation, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I would like to go back to the incidents which you said was the opening of the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to please go to Exhibit P466.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, that's, again, your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like the registry to turn to page 45 of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, what I would wish do to with you is to go chronologically with you through a particular part of your report, where you have listed what you called "NLA operations." That's the part 2.11 of your report, and it would be at the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please, that's page 46 of the report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to go, as I said, chronologically with you in relation to these matters. Under the heading "January 2001," and as far as concerns "NLA operations," you list the following incident, and I will read it out to you: "The first incident attributed to the NLA was a mortar attack on a remote police station at Tearce on 22 January 2001. Unknown assailants attacked the police station, killing one policeman and wounding three." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's the same attack, isn't it, or operation, as you name it, that you read later in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that this incident in Tearce occurred sometime during the night between the 21st and 22nd of January of 2001? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember reading various accounts, including those in media, and I think it probably occurred during night.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know how many members of the NLA took part in this particular operation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know of any approximation, or is it information that is totally unknown to you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I wouldn't make any guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know how long the attack lasted, this attack on the police station?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the attack resulted in at least one person killed and several persons wounded. In fact, it doesn't really matter how long this attack lasted, as long as actually it achieved its primary goal, delivering casualties on the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I will just ask to you answer the question if you can; if you can't, please say so. Do you know how long the attack lasted?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that, as far as the reports are concerned, it only involved the firing of one mortar, which I think -- or one shell, in any case, on to the police station in Tearce. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accounts which I have seen, sir, seem to suggest that there was a mortar as well as grenade launchers used.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated already that there was one casualty and three injured persons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As was clear from the media reports, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that on that occasion, the NLA did not capture any territory as a result of that attack. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I simply was not looking into this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know where this men or man who had been carrying out the attack had been coming from?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read various materials and lots of various materials, of course, and it would be difficult to keep in mind all the names of possible suspects which were speculated in with media materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know how and where they retreated to?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember seeing various reports suggesting that, in fact, the assailants withdrew to the territory of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know whether they had used any communication facilities during that incident?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not really investigating this particular attack, sir, but I would imagine that they probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you see any documentary evidence of any plan to carry out this attack?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you see any documentary evidence of an order to carry out this attack?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, and, again, as far as you can recall, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this particular incident, this particular attack on the police station, was regarded and called a terrorist act or a terrorist action by the Macedonian authorities? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Macedonian authorities, by and large, as I can see from various Macedonian documents, regarded the NLA as terrorists; and, in fact, this is how the NLA was treated in various Macedonian documents. They mentioned as enemy and terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you have any memory of this particular -- well, let me perhaps show what you what is Rule 65 ter 1D873. Mr. Bezruchenko, we'll come back on a few occasions on this document, but are you familiar, first, with this document, which is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that this is a information on the NLA activities in the territory of Macedonia, that it's dated the 25th of July of 2001, and it comes from the Department of Security and Counter-Intelligence, also known as the UBK? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could turn to page 7 of this document, that would be 1D00-7639.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you see, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this document contains what is termed, "A chronology ever terrorist attacks." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go to the fifth incident mentioned in this document, it starts with the word: "In the night." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says this: "In the night between January 21 and 22, 2001, the Tearce police station in -- came under an automatic gun-fire and hand-rocket launcher attack. Stojanovski Momir was killed, while Evrosimovski Davor, Lika Jahi, and Gjurovski Borce were seriously wounded. "In its communique number 4, dated January 23rd, NLA assumed responsibility for this attack." First, do you agree that this is the same incident as we discussed before?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it appears so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that it is being listed by the UBK as a terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please now be shown what is Exhibit P45, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, first, I think you will be quite familiar with this document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is known as the "White Book" prepared by the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also made use of that particular document in various parts of your original report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I ask the registry to turn to page 109 of that document, please. Thank you. That be would be the next page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that this particular section of the "White Book" refers to terrorist attacks and provocation carried out by the so-called NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to go down to the third incident listed as activity attack, there is a date of the 22nd of January of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And prior to that you have two incidents, one dated the 11th of January of 2000 and the 19th of January of 2000. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the incident listed under 22nd of January of 2001 reads as follows: "The police station Tearce, Tetovo was attacked with a hand-grenade mortar and an automatic weapon and hit with two projectiles. The police officer, Momir Stojanovski, was killed and three other police officers suffered severe body injuries. Material damages were caused, too. "By a communique number 4 presented on January 23, 2001, NLA took the responsibility for this terrorist attack. According to the communique, a special unit of the NLA committed the attack against the police station Tearce." Do you agree that, again, this is the same incident which we have been discussing? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, also, that according to the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia, this particular incident constituted a terrorist attack, as it's termed?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what the document says. Indeed, the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia apparently considered all these attacks terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that for yourself, Mr. Bezruchenko, when you identified references to terrorist attacks or terrorists to describe the NLA, you suggested quite a different explanation? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to my specific use of the word "operations," Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, I apologise. Perhaps I should, in fairness, show you the passage that I'm referring to in your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could bring back P466, please, and if I may ask the registry, please, to turn to page 87 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this will be paragraph 299 of the report, page 87.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask to you look at paragraph 299 of the report, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In your report you said the following: "It should be noted that operational documents of the Macedonian Ministry of Defence and General Staff, especially operational orders, refer to the NLA as 'terrorists' and the 'enemy.' "From this, one can infer that despite the fact that no formal state of war was declared, the army was in effect at a heightened state of readiness and that orders and instructions were generated according to the threat posed by activity enemy forces." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ever consider the possibility, Mr. Bezruchenko, anywhere in your report, that the reason why the NLA was called "terrorists" was because that's what they were?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may offer the following comment, Mr. Mettraux: The phenomenon of terrorism is not an easy one to understand, and there are various definitions of terrorism which have been a subject of debate, both in the academic community around the world and in various international bodies including the United Nations. You may wish to recall that attempts to somehow bring these definitions to one common denominator, so to speak, have, to this point in time, not really yielded any results. There are various explanations and various definitions of the phenomenon of terrorism. There are some which are apparently more acceptable than others, but one common feature or as one common point about all these definitions is that terrorism, as such, as phenomenon, is essentially an action aimed at civilians, rather than military or government structures. In this sense, a typical example of terrorism, perhaps, would be an attack on a school in Beslam [Realtime transcript read in error "Islam"], as well as the 9/11. But in my report, I was not really dealing with the issue of terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, I'm grateful for your explanation, Mr. Bezruchenko. The answer to the question is that, in fact, and I believe that's what you said in your last sentence, you did not consider the possibility in your report that the NLA was, in fact, a terrorist organisation and that its actions, in fact, were terrorist attacks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As is evident from the chronology, which is section 5 of my report, Mr. Mettraux, I have been dealing with mostly attacks by the NLA against the army and police. In the course of preparation of my report, I did not really find any overwhelming evidence to suggest that, say, the major part of such attacks, or rather, the most of these attacks were specifically aimed at civilian population. In fact, if this were the case, the number of casualties resulting in the conflict would probably be much, much higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this then, Mr. Bezruchenko: As part of your review and identification of documents relevant to the preparation of your report, did you become aware of any and perhaps numerous statements from various state and state bodies to the effect that the NLA was a terrorist organisation or that its actions were terrorist acts? Did you become aware of any such material?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we come over to this question, Mr. Mettraux, if I may correct a mistake, apparently, which is on the transcript. I said, on the attack on the school in "Beslam," not "Islam."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is B-E-S-L-A-M.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, and this is line 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you wish me to repeat the question, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The question was this: As part of your review of the documents relevant to the preparation of your report, did you become aware of any and perhaps numerous statements from various states and state bodies to the effect that the NLA was a terrorist organisation or that its actions were terrorist acts.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were numerous statements which suggested that, in fact, terrorist acts were being committed in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that you made no reference in your report to any such material? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. In fact, the numerous documents which I'm quoting, including the documents of the General Staff for instance, directly name the NLA as terrorists and the enemy. I think there are other documents as well, especially in the media, which essentially say the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I should have specified my question better, Mr. Bezruchenko. Did you make any reference in your report to statements or report of statement made by other state or other state organs, setting aside, for a second, statements made by the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the statements of international mediators, politicians, heads of states regarding the situation in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I was not concentrating on this because apparently this would represent the political aspect of the conflict and political interpretation of it, which was not really my interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour? It's only half past, I'm sorry. I was ahead of myself. Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D928.1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is, again, the same document, the DoD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record, we have uploaded a slightly different document with a ".1" because we have added one page that is relevant to the document. So we have re-uploaded the entire document. And if I could ask the registry, please, to go to page 1D00-8274 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'll ask you, first, to look at the definition that is given of the concept of terrorism in this particular document, and I will read it out to you: "Terrorism - the calculated use of unlawful violence or threat of unlawful violence to instill fear, intended to coerce or to intimidate governments or societies in the pursuit of goals that are generally political, religious, or ideological." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that there is no reference to any targeting of civilians. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see there is no such reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the next definition, that of terrorist, it says this: "An individual who commits an act or acts of violence or threatens violence in pursuit of political, religious, or ideological objectives." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a definition of what constitutes a terrorist group, and it is defined as follows: "Any number of terrorists who assemble together have a unifying relationship or are organised for the purpose of committing an act or acts of violence or threatened violence in pursuant of their political, religious, or ideological objective." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, you agree that this particular military definition of the concept of terrorist group does not contain any reference or any limitation to attacks on civilians. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, in effect, Mr. Bezruchenko, you did not apply this particular set of definition as were provided in the DoD Military Dictionary of military terms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really find this particular definition particularly explanatory. Well, in fact, the pursuit of political, religious, or ideological goals is not necessarily exercised through terrorism only. The war remains the major vehicle for pursuit of such goals. Secondly, this particular definition does not seem to be intended to making a distinction between war and terrorism; and, thirdly, in fact, this definition does notice really preclude the use of force against civilians, as it speaks of the societies.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it also speaks of the governments. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since societies are run by governments.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, Mr. Bezruchenko, what you are saying then is, whilst you rely on the definition of what constitutes an armed conflict on this document, you decided that other definitions in that document were not appropriate for your own purposes and did not apply this particular definitions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned, Mr. Mettraux, first and foremost, in the first place, the phenomenon of terrorism was not really the subject of my report. I was researching in my report the matters which were directly related to the conflict, such as organisation of the opposing sides, strategy, tactics, and all the other issues. Terrorism is a special phenomenon. It does not necessarily mean that the war in Macedonia in 2001 was not a war in which terrorist acts were not involved; perhaps they were. But the overwhelming fact remains that essentially, by and large, this was the clash between the organised forces of the government, on the one hand, and the organised forces of the of the NLA, on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, you knew much more than what you are now claiming. You knew about the relevance of terrorism to what you were asked to prepare. Isn't that correct that you knew full well that acts of terrorism would be excluded from the definition of armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand your question, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that at the time when you prepared your report, it was made clear to you, by your colleagues who are lawyers, that acts of terrorism are excluded from the definition of what constitutes an armed conflict, and that such acts cannot serve as evidence of the existence of an armed conflict? Do you agree that was made clear to you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you, Mr. Mettraux. And, on the other hand, does it actually mean that you are suggesting that there was no armed conflict in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for the time being, I would like to stay with the question, Mr. Bezruchenko, if we may. Is it your evidence that you were not informed by the Office of the Prosecutor, by your colleagues, that terrorist actions would be excluded from the definition of what constitutes an armed conflict in law?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is my evidence, Mr. Mettraux, because I don't think that we discussed specifically the relationship between the phenomenon of terrorism and the armed conflict; and, secondly, as I mentioned previously, I did not really have in my mind any legal concept of the conflict when I was writing my report. What I was guided by, specific request which was indeed provided to me by my colleagues and which covered such issues as organisation of the parties, religious tactics, and all these things which I have already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, did you watch the opening statement of the Prosecution in this case?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to read a passage to you from that opening statement delivered by Mr. Saxon. It's at page 327 of the transcript on the 16th of April of 2007. Mr. Saxon was discussing the particular issue of the existence or otherwise of an armed conflict in Macedonia at the time, and these are the words of Mr. Saxon: "First of all, the Prosecution must prove that there was sufficient organisation and structure of the belligerent armed forces, so that each participating force had the ability to carry out military operations. "Second, the Prosecution must demonstrate that the intensity of the armed violence or combat, if you will, rose to a certain level; that is, that the level of armed violence was something greater than mere banditry, common crime, or disorganised or short-lived insurrection, or terrorist activities which are not the subject to the international humanitarian law," and Mr. Saxon goes on to discuss other elements of that definition. Mr. Bezruchenko, are you suggesting, or is that your evidence, that you were not aware at the time of preparing your statement of the definition and the elements and in particular the relevance of terrorist activities to that definition. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, of course, I was watching the statement, the opening statement which was made by Mr. Saxon. But, as I mentioned previously already, by the time this statement was actually made, my report had been, by and large, completed. So I don't really think there is any direct connection between this statement and my report. This is the first point I would like to make. Now, coming to the second point of your question is regarding the terrorist activities. I have got an impression throughout getting ready with my report, and actually in the process of writing my report, that there was, indeed, a lot of crime committed during the conflict in Macedonia. But, again, coming back, if you wish, to the qualification provided by Mr. Saxon, I would concur with the view that it was not really banditry or short-lived insurrection. NLA was a organised entity which was manifested, inter alia, in the fact they had military hierarchy, as well as very solid political goals, which in fact are also a reflection of an armed conflict, and these goals were, in fact, solidified and expressed in the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. The Chamber would be quite aware of your evidence in relation to there matter, but I'd like to come back dot issue of terrorism, if I may. Is it your evidence that the Prosecutor, who asked you to prepare a report on the issue of the existence of an armed conflict in Macedonia in the year of 2001, did not bring to your attention this definition, which goes back to the Tadic judgment of, I believe, 1997 and onwards, that the Prosecutor did not bring that definition, in particular as regard terrorist activities, to your attention. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not read Tadic's judgment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko, but my question is broader than that. Is it your evidence that the content, the substance of what I read to you a moment ago, was not brought to your attention at the time when you prepared your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously, we were discussing my report, of course, but I was given complete freedom as how I was supposed to structure it and carry on with it. We only discussed the plan, but the substantive matters, such as organisation of the parties, as well as the operations and the main events, were not really the subject of these discussions. So if your specific question is whether I was specifically instructed to avoid anything in relation to terrorism in my report, this is -- my answer to this question is no, I was not instructed so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we have one minute, Mr. Bezruchenko. I was not suggesting and I was not asking whether you had been instructed to avoid making any such reference. My question was: Is it your evidence that the content or substance of what I read to you a moment ago was not brought to your attention at the time when you prepared your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would it be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, just a last point on the discussion which we had before the break. It is more a matter of methodology to understand how you proceeded and if my understanding of your methodology is correct. Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you did not seek to determine for each or any particular incident whether that particular incident was or wasn't a terrorism act? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not looking into the aspect of terrorism at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. I have some more general questions about the NLA and the NLA structure in relation to the month of January of 2001, Mr. Bezruchenko. Did you see any documentary evidence about the numbers of members of the NLA in January of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is extremely difficult to make any assessment as to the actual numbers of the NLA. In fact, to this date, there have been very few statements suggesting that the size of the NLA amounted to a certain number of men. I think I have seen documents suggesting that there were various groups, mostly coming from Kosovo, but also supported by some local population which amounted perhaps to a few hundred men in January.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct or is it within your knowledge that the number 30 persons, 100 and 200 were sometimes mentioned? Is it within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These numbers were mentioned, that's right; but as I say, it is very difficult to make any accurate assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Have you seen any documentary evidence concerning, again, Mr. Bezruchenko, the month of January of 2001, suggesting that any of the so-called NLA brigade had been set up at that time and was operating in January of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically related to any NLA brigade set up in January 2001, no, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you see any order with the stamp or any other identification from any of those so-called brigades as far as concerned the month of January of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you see any map -- did you see any map of operation that were used for the purpose of the NLA in January of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a issue, Mr. Bezruchenko, which I would like to touch with you again in relation to the NLA. Is it correct that - and as far as I could tell from the report - one of the issue which is not discussed in your report is the NLA's deployment or transport facilities and abilities? Is that correct that you do not discuss that particular aspect of the NLA structure?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not really pursuing this specific subject in detail, but I think I refer to a number of documents which relate to transportation routes across the border from Kosovo and various transport facilities. At least under the subtitle of "Logistics," I think I speak about transport routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that. At this stage, I'm more interested in the vehicles themselves, to say that. Are you aware of the NLA having had any means -- well, let me put it differently. Are you aware that the NLA had any vehicle or trucks, for instance, to be used in the month of January of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not really recall seeing any document suggesting that any vehicles were used in the month of January 2001, but I certainly recall a number of documents which suggest that, generally speaking, NLA was using mainly tractors, but perhaps also some vehicles. But I'm not sure if this was limited exclusively to January 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the deployment ability of any army formation would be relevant, for instance, to the type of operation which this formation would be capable of carrying out?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it would also be directly relevant to determining the kind of forces or the number of forces that such a formation would be capable of transporting from one location to the other. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it would also be relevant to determining the sort of armament that this formation would be capable of transporting from one site to the other. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In conventional warfare, mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it would be also be relevant to establishing the ability of that formation to carry out more than short-lived attacks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what is your definition of "short-lived attacks," sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, is it correct that should any such formation wish to carry out an attack that could last for, let's say, more than a few days, it would be important to ensure the means of re-supply? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, attack is only a form of combat activities. Other forms of combat activity also include defence and, among other things , actions as ways of implementing them. But if your specific question is whether re-supply would determine the duration of a particular operation, yes, of course, it would be one of the major factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in turn, the ability to re-supply troops would be determined, in part, at least, by the ability of the formation in question to transport that re-supply. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are various ways, of course, of carrying out re-supply activities. I mean, it really depends on what you mean. In conventional warfare, yes. Normally, a unit would be responsible for its re-supplies up to a certain level.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I believe, if can you recall, you were shown one document during your examination-in-chief which suggested that at the end of the crisis, the NLA was in possession of four vehicles which were armoured vehicles and tanks. Do you recall that those vehicles were taken from or off the Macedonian forces during the crisis?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think they were taken from the Macedonian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know of any other vehicle which the NLA possessed in January of 2001 and during the rest of the crisis which they used for the purpose of transporting troops?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously, there are some reports which suggest that they were using tractors, especially carrying weapons across the border, as well as perhaps trucks. But if you are specifically referring to any combat vehicles, except those which had been captured by the NLA, no, I don't think I came across any references to such vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you see any evidence of the NLA possessing any trucks, not just combat vehicles, but trucks; and if so, did you refer to that particular information in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I refer to this particular information in my report, but I remember seeing some report suggesting that perhaps they had trucks. But I'm not really sure. It wasn't really the focus of my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that a great deal of transportation or movement by the NLA was done on foot and the carrying of loads on mules or donkeys? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this would mean that the movement of the troops would be extremely slow. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in turn, this would limit the type of operations that the NLA would be capable of carrying out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and no. It really depends. Apparently, there could be some situations whereby the NLA did not really have to deploy large amount of forces in certain areas, since the personnel were already there, just infiltrated over a number of years -- sorry, number of days, perhaps weeks or months. The weapons could be just hid there, waiting for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I hope you can agree with the proposition that this means of transportation, foot and mules, would greatly restrain the scope of possible operations that could be carried out by this body. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This would be very logical to assume, but, as I say, it really applies mainly to conventional warfare. That not be necessarily the same situation in asymmetrical warfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree that it would also restrict the number of troops that could be deployed at any one time in relation to any one particular operation? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of the reason for that would be that they would easily become identifiable, or otherwise. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the NLA having had any common vehicles with communication facilities in the month of January of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that the vehicles which were used in Aracinovo to evacuate NLA fighters from the village were those of NATO? Is that correct? Is it within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the absence of such vehicles and assistance to evacuate, the only way for the NLA people to get out of the village would have been on foot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that in January of 2001, the attacks which you've described in your report, the attacks of the NLA against the Macedonian forces, were regarded as a low-level affair? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You really have to specify your question, Mr. Mettraux. I would rather prefer if you could explain who are you attributing these reports to and where they would be coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, first, let me ask you this then: Do you agree that the situation in Macedonia at the time, and in particular the one attack that you described in your report, was a low intensity affair?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, in a way, the entire conflict could perhaps be described as a conflict of medium intensity, I would say. But at the beginning of the conflict, I think, there certainly was a tendency for - this is what would appear, in fact, from various media reports - for the Macedonian authorises to regard this conflict as not really significant, something which probably could be dealt with very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Bezruchenko, of a magazine called "Jane's Intelligence Digest"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that you relied upon various publication from Jane's in preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like to show you one particular piece from Jane's Intelligence Digest.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Exhibit 1D227, and if it could be scrolled down a little bit more, please, to the beginning of the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing that article, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I have seen this article, but I probably -- I probably did; at least I have seen some similar articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the first paragraph of this article first. It says this: "Current events in the Balkans indicate that Jane's Intelligence Digest oft repeated warnings of an escalating series of regional conflicts are proving accurate. In the space of a week, ethnic Albanian terrorists have launched an attack on a Macedonian police station," and then it goes on to speak about Kosovo. First, let me ask you this: Is it correct that the NLA is described also by Jane's as ethnic Albanian terrorists? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it refers specifically to an attack on a Macedonian police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph, Jane's say this is: "All of these incidents have a common root: Radical Albanian nationalism." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, I'll ask you to locate a paragraph which starts with the word: "The low-level." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is what Jane's says: "The low-level attacks against the Macedonian police, which began last year, are supposedly the work of the so-called Liberation Army, four of whom have been arrested." Do you agree that at this stage, at the time of the article which is 2nd of February but posted on the 1st of February, the Jane's Intelligence Digest regarded what was happening in Macedonia as low-level attacks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this article is dated to January 2001 --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: February, I'm sorry, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: February, okay. Indeed, in January and February 2001, there was a number of clashes. There was some fighting going on, but it didn't really spread out towards the territory which later came under NLA control. Basically, the fighting was limited to certain areas on the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that what Jane's refers to is that there were in fact other similar attacks in the year -- the previous year? That would be the year of 2000. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that, in fact, attacks by members of various groups with various names, Albanian armed groups of various sorts, had been going on since at least 1992 onwards? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, attacks, in a sense of attacks against military and police, well, I don't think so. I know that there were various incidents here and there. There were some bombings as well, but there were indeed various groups involved in these attacks. But my concept of the conflict was that in earnest the fighting between the NLA and the Macedonian security forces began, in fact, in January and February, and one of the reasons for this concept is that this particular attack, on the 28th of January, was confirmed by the NLA statement. They actually assumed responsibility for this attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that, in fact, the only thing that changed between 2001 and the year 2000, or the year of 1999, is simply the number of and frequency of those attacks? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be fair to say perhaps that the amount of the attacks increased significantly in February 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just wrapping it up for the month of January of 2001, Mr. Bezruchenko, is it your expert evidence that the incidents which we've discussed, the incident of Tearce that may have lasted only a few minutes, that might have involved a unknown number of people, perhaps two, three, without any apparent plan of order for it, and with one casualty would be enough in your experience to amount to an armed conflict in military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be grateful, Mr. Mettraux, if you would indicate in a specific location in my report where I made this assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, your evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, as far as I understand it, is that this incident, and you indicated earlier today, marked the beginning of what you called an armed conflict. Now, I understand from that evidence that it is your position that this incident was in and of itself sufficient to amount or to give rise to an armed conflict in Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. Mettraux, you are simply misrepresenting what I said. I said that this incident was the first one in the series of attacks which later amounted to what turned out to be a full-fledged conflict of serious intensity. I said that the first incident, but I didn't really say, as you are putting to me now, that this incident amount to an armed conflict. This is entirely wrong, and this is gross misrepresentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, your evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you gave to this Chamber is that the beginning of the armed conflict, which you said lasted from January 2001 until September 2001, started on the 22nd of January 2001 with this incident. Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that the conflict actually started in January, that's right, specifically because it is in January that the reports about the NLA existence came to the attention of the media, and the NLA assumed the responsibility for some incidents. But I don't really think that I that I say that this specific incident amounted to the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the record will speak for itself. I will turn to the month of February of 2001, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to bring back what is Exhibit P466, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, that will be your report, once again, and I will ask you now to turn to page 46, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask you, please, to turn to paragraph 169 of that report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that is the operations which -- NLA operations which you list as being relevant for the month of February 2001, and I will read them out to you: "On 21 February 2001, Macedonian border security reported movement of about 40 persons in black and camouflage uniforms crossing the border from FRY into Macedonia. "The border agreement signed by Macedonia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on 23 February prompted the army to move its unit up to the newly proclaimed border line. That move led to clashes in the area of Tanusevci on the border between Macedonia and Kosovo in February 2001, as NLA attempted to hold and expand the bridgehead which would enable them to control the difficult to access Skopska-Crna Gora area as a base for further operations." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, focussing on those clashes which you refer in the fifth line of that particular paragraph, do you know how long that particular incident lasted?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the clashes in the area of Tanusevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was a recurrent affair. I think initially it lasted for about a day, but then the area was confronted again, and the incident reoccurred sometime in March. I don't think this area was really quiet until the very end of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the transcript -- well, I will do that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you know how many members of the so-called NLA were involved in what you described as clashes in the area of Tanusevci on border between Macedonia and Kosovo in February 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it be would difficult to give you the precise figure, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so that the Chamber has an idea of the scale of things in this matter and the sort of event we are talking about, is that correct that the village of Tanusevci is about or the area around the village of Tanusevci is about six square kilometre? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is indeed a small village, but I don't know what is the exact surface of this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can assist you, since I haven't measured it myself, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask that the registry bring up Exhibit P45, and if the registry could please turn to page 65 of that document, please. That would be N000-9317. That would not be the right page. Could we move two page forward, please. Yes, thank you very much. And if we can go down to the last paragraph of that document, please, and if we can focus on the last paragraph of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see that? It starts with the word: "Allow me to remind you."

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that the area which is referred to as having been occupied in relation to these activities is said to be six square kilometres of the village Tanusevci? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tanusevci, sir. Yes, indeed, this is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
