utterances.text: I'm grateful, and I apologise for the pronunciation. Are aware, Mr. Bezruchenko, of any combat casualties which occurred during the event in the village or in or around the village, Tanusevci?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were some casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing it in any document; and if so, did you it anywhere in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you perhaps could give the exact date, I could find the appropriate sentence, paragraph in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could back to Mr. Bezruchenko's report at page 46, please, this is Exhibit P466.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, this would be page 46 of your report, paragraph 169, please. Is it correct that in your report, Mr. Bezruchenko, and unlike what is the case in other circumstances where there were casualties, you do not suggest that any casualties occurred during those clashes? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I may not have suggested this in this particular paragraph, and, in fact, it is not really -- it was not really my intention, but I think the issue of casualties was covered in greater detail in the section 5 of my report, where I speak about the chronology.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know what sort of weapons or weaponry the NLA was using at the time in February of 2001 in the course of the clashes which were taking place in the area of Tanusevci?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to various reports, these were mostly small arms weapons, like automatic rifles, but apparently also various machine-guns, grenade launchers, and mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that at the time these activities, these attacks of the NLA in the area around or near Tanusevci, were characterised again as criminal or in some cases extremist or terrorist attacks? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the Macedonian authorities were consistent in describing these attack as terrorist acts throughout the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree there was never any suggestions on the part of the Macedonian authorities, less stay with February at that stage, that there was no suggestion by the Macedonian authorities in February 2001 that what they were involved was an armed conflict? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. Macedonian authorities perhaps did not really admit this fact, but it does not necessarily mean that the conflict was not going on. And, again, if you refer to the Macedonian military experts, specifically, the book which you have already mentioned several times, they share the view that the conflict actually began in February. So, essentially, my views and the views of these experts concur with minor differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the experts to whom you refer are these experts to whom you did not talk to. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D879, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a address of the president of the government of the Republic of Macedonia, his Excellency Mr. Ljubco Georgievski, and it relates to a summit that took place in Skopje on February 22nd and 23rd of 2001. I would like to draw your attention in particular to a paragraph which starts with the word, "In the recent few weeks." Can you locate that? This is the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will read it out to you: "In the recent few weeks, the Republic of Macedonia has, unfortunately, been facing an aggression on the part of Albanian extremist groups, seriously endangering its sovereignty and territorial integrity, but also the peace stability and security of the Balkans and Europe." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could turn, please, to the next page, and if the registry could focus on the middle of the page which starts with the words, "Ladies and Gentlemen," please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is still the address of the prime minister, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I will read it out for you. It says this: "At the current moment, when south-eastern Europe is again facing another crisis being a consequence of recent actions on the part of Albanian extremist terrorist groups, bringing again to the surface the greater state projects in the Balkans, even greater is the importance of all forms of regional interlinkage and cooperation. "I would like to stress that the Republic of Macedonia will decisively deal with all forms of terrorism violence and extremism, and will not allow the endangering of the basic values and principles upon which our state lies." Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this statement of the prime minister of the time, Mr. Ljubco Georgievski, pretty much reflects the position of the Macedonian authorities at the time, that what they were involved in is a fight against terrorism, violence, and extremism?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, sir. I don't really see any reason not to disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as of the month of February of 2001, is it also correct that you did not identify -- or I should put it differently to you. Did you identify any statement made by any one state or state authorities as of February 2001 that suggested that the events in Macedonia amounted to an armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Amounted to an armed conflict," just for the record. As of February 2001, no, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And let me ask you a few general questions about the state of the so-called NLA at that point, in February 2001. Are you aware of any documentary evidence that would suggest that in February of 2001, NLA brigades had been set up and were operating in February of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I think that perhaps the first NLA brigade to set up was the NLA 113th Brigade -- sorry, 112th Brigade which was operating in the area of Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall perhaps when that brigade was set up, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any specific documents which would suggest any specific date.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now for the day and resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 31st day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
